doc.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Leaving studio work and the lip surgery layoff
summary: He quit studio work over flute demands and stopped playing about fifteen years after jaw surgery.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah. I stopped doing studio work in the early 60s when all the commercial people started requiring saxophone players to play flute, and since I was writing and everything I figured I didn’t really want to take time to learn to play the flute, so that kind of went down. And then in the 60s I had some surgery on my jaw and my lip, they cut some nerves and my lip lost its strength, so I just quit playing then for about 15 years until I started my band again, and then I wanted to be able to participate, so I got the horn out and it kind of worked. The lip had come back somewhat so I was able to play a little bit. And a few years later I had some dental implants put in and they blew the nerves again, so currently I don’t have a whole lot of strength in my lip, but I’m working on it because I still want to be able to participate with the band.
